assets.notes: blargg (Shay Green) SNES SPC700/APU test ROMs. They report results via blargg's standard text shell (Passed / Failed #N / Internal error), so the committed subset is verified by comparing the rendered screen CRC32 at a fixed frame against a human-approved PASS capture (NESER_CAPTURE_SCREEN). License is informal: these are freely-redistributable test binaries with no formal license file, recorded as unknown; author site http://www.slack.net/~ant/. All 18 ROMs are committed and all 18 currently PASS in this emulator with visually-approved screen-CRC goldens, one test per ROM (blargg_rom_test! in blargg_apu_tests.rs). timer_at_power_reset requires a mid-test soft reset when the ROM jumps to $0000 (modeled via RunConfig::with_reset_on_pc_trap); spc_dsp6 needs an extended 600M-tick budget and runs to frame 9100. See README-SNES for details.

variants.notes: All 18 blargg SPC700/APU ROMs have visually-approved PASS goldens run by snes::integration_tests::blargg_apu_tests with the screen-CRC oracle, one test per ROM.

assets.notes: undisbeliever (Marcus Rowe) SNES hardware-glitch/timing-hammer test ROMs. Unlike blargg/gilyon, these do not print a PASS/FAIL text screen -- most demonstrate a real, documented hardware bug (the 'INIDISP D7 glitch': writing $2100 shortly after the CPU/HDMA data bus held a byte with bit 7 set can corrupt sprite rendering or briefly flip force-blank on real 3-chip/1-chip consoles; see the NESdev post quoted at https://github.com/akatsuki105/snes-test-roms/tree/master/undisbeliever-inidisp, from Near/byuu, with real-hardware reference photos) or are interactive demos. No known SNES emulator models this glitch -- checked Mesen2, ares (Near's own current emulator), and Snes9x, all write $2100 deterministically with no bus-residual modeling (issue #2949). 12 of the 29 vendored ROMs are automated: each golden is a stability snapshot cross-checked against a Mesen2 capture (using --Video.VideoFilter=None --Video.AspectRatio=NoStretching, and allowing for a harmless constant 1-scanline row offset between the two emulators' screenshot conventions). For 2 of the 12 (hdma-21ff-glitch.sfc, inidisp_hammer_0f0f.sfc) the source confirms real hardware never glitches, so those goldens genuinely are hardware-accurate; for the other 9 (hdma-2100-glitch.sfc, hdma-21ff-2100-0f-glitch.sfc, inidisp_d7_glitch_test.sfc, inidisp_hammer_0f.sfc, inidisp_hammer_0f00.sfc, inidisp_hammer_0f8f.sfc, inidisp_hammer_0f8f_fast.sfc, inidisp_hammer_0f_long.sfc, inidisp_hammer_8f0f.sfc) real hardware usually glitches and the golden only proves parity with a limitation shared by every checked reference emulator (issue #2949), not hardware accuracy. inidisp_enable_display_mid_frame.sfc is unrelated to the D7 glitch and is confirmed hardware-accurate. See snes::integration_tests::undisbeliever_tests. The other 17 ROMs showed real NESER-vs-Mesen2 divergences during cross-checking and are deliberately left un-automated pending fixes: hdmaen_latch_test(_2).sfc, inidisp_brightness_delay.sfc, hdma-2100-glitch-2ch-{0a,81}.sfc, hdma-21ff-2100-glitch.sfc (issue #2943, likely finer within-scanline HDMA timing than the once-per-scanline model added for #2945/#2947 covers); inidisp_forgot_to_force_blank.sfc (issue #2944, missing VRAM/OAM corruption from writes outside force-blank); all 10 scpu-a-dma-bug-*.sfc (issue #2945, the break/COP crash is fixed but the HDMA-driven scanline-brightness banding isn't yet phase-accurate against Mesen2). See README-SNES.md for the full breakdown.

variants.notes: All 29 ROMs are vendored; 12 have visually-approved stability-snapshot goldens run by snes::integration_tests::undisbeliever_tests with the screen-CRC oracle, one test per ROM. The remaining 17 are committed but not yet automated (see notes above and #2943/#2944/#2945).

assets.notes: Two ROMs (hvdma.sfc, hvdma_max.sfc) from a NESdev forum post by user '93143' (https://forums.nesdev.com/viewtopic.php?p=248408#p248408), mirrored into the rmstdope/snes-test-roms fork of higan's bundled test ROMs (not a dedicated per-author ROM-source repo, hence license unknown -- no LICENSE file exists in the submodule root or this subfolder). Neither prints a PASS/FAIL text screen; both are cross-checked against Mesen2 captures of the identical ROM file, same methodology as the undisbeliever suite. 1 of 2 is automated: hvdma.sfc (all 8 HDMA channels force-blank/write-VRAM-address/burst-20-bytes/unblank on two scanlines, changing BG1's tile pattern partway down the screen) now matches both Mesen2 and the bundled real-hardware reference photo after fixing #2952 (NESER's HDMA transfer mode 5 was reusing general-purpose DMA's cyclic-mode simplification, truncating 4 bytes/line to 2 and desyncing the per-channel HDMA table pointer, so every VMDATA channel mistook a leftover data byte for the table terminator right after its first line). hvdma_max.sfc (an H-IRQ-triggered DMA burst probing force-blank release timing) renders solid black in NESER vs. Mesen2's documented solid green -- a real, separate rendering gap unaffected by the #2952 fix, tracked as #2953 and deliberately left un-automated. See snes::integration_tests::hblank_dma_vram_tests and README-SNES.md.

variants.notes: Both ROMs are vendored; hvdma.sfc has a visually-approved, Mesen2-cross-checked golden run by snes::integration_tests::hblank_dma_vram_tests with the screen-CRC oracle. hvdma_max.sfc is committed but not yet automated pending #2953.

assets.notes: absindx SA-1 conformance ROMs (epic #2956), verified with human-approved screen-CRC goldens like the blargg/gilyon suites. Both ROMs are documented (and separately confirmed) to behave unreliably on Mesen2, so the goldens are navigator-approved captures of NESER's own rendering (NESER_CAPTURE_SCREEN=1), not Mesen2 cross-checks. Both settle into static result screens (SNES CPU in its WAI idle loop, SA-1 parked in SA1TestFinished_InfLoop), so a fixed-frame CRC is stable (verified identical at frames 150 and 250). SA1RamProtectionTest.sfc: all 222 sub-tests PASS; the golden captures the 'Result Passed' screen (TEST ID 222, SRAM $020000). SA1VersionCodeTest.sfc: the golden captures the hardware-accurate register-dump screen whose result line reads 'Failed' even on real hardware -- disassembly proves its CheckResult unconditionally takes the failed path (the pass path at $9EAB is unreferenced dead code), deliberate since the true SA-1 version-code value is unknown (fullsnes) and $230E is open bus (bsnes). See snes::integration_tests::sa1_absindx_tests and README-SNES.md.

variants.notes: Prebuilt SA1RamProtectionTest.sfc/SA1VersionCodeTest.sfc (+ .sym files) from the upstream release page, plus the SNES-TestRoms source subtree. Both ROMs have visually-approved screen-CRC goldens run by snes::integration_tests::sa1_absindx_tests, one test per ROM.

assets.notes: gilyon/snes-tests 65816 CPU and SPC-700 test ROMs, vendored as a git-subtree mirror plus prebuilt ROMs (replacing the earlier ad-hoc gilyon_tests/ copy; see issue #2979). cputest.sfc is the full 1610-test 65816 build (bit-identical to the previously vendored cputest-full.sfc, so its golden carried over; the retired 1107-test cputest-basic.sfc was a strict subset and its separate test was dropped). spctest.sfc is a newer upstream build with 1320 SPC-700 tests (the older vendored build had 1368; count changed upstream). Both report results via a text shell (Success / Failed #N with register dump), verified by the rom_runner screen-CRC oracle against human-approved PASS captures; both currently PASS -- one test per ROM in snes::integration_tests::gilyon_cpu_tests / gilyon_spc_tests.

variants.notes: Prebuilt cputest.sfc and spctest.sfc plus the snes-tests source subtree.

assets.notes: Deterministic S-DSP-level golden windows over synthetic BRR fixtures covering BRR decode, ADSR, GAIN, pitch modulation, echo/FIR, gaussian interpolation, mixing/clamping, and the noise LFSR. Baselines are per-window CRC32 metadata (sample rate, warmup/window lengths, fixture source, review note) inline in the Rust test source. WAV review artifacts are generated on demand with NESER_CAPTURE_AUDIO=1 under target/snes_test_captures/dsp_audio_golden_tests/ and are never committed.

variants.notes: No on-disk assets; fixtures and approved CRC baselines live in dsp_audio_golden_tests.rs within this directory.
